option.counterfactual: The existence of a nonlinear normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor is sufficient to construct a sequence satisfying all the conditions defining some member of G.
option.approach: Start from a failure of additivity on two positive elements and investigate whether it can be repeated in equivalent corners of the factor. The goal would be to turn a finite additivity defect into infinitely many positive increments inside a bounded order interval.

belief.answer: An exact determination is currently open. In particular, \(\boxed{\mathcal G=\varnothing\iff\text{every normalized }2\text{-quasitrace on every finite }\mathrm{AW}^*\text{-factor is linear}}\), the quasitracial formulation of Kaplansky’s conjecture. Unconditionally, \(\mathcal G\subseteq(0,\tfrac12]\) and \(\mathcal G\) is downward closed.

judge.reason: It makes concrete claims: an equivalence with a conjecture, an upper bound, and downward closure, while asserting the exact determination is open. This differs from each earlier answer, all of which prescribe a specific set.
judge.gate: The proposed answer gives only an equivalence with an unproved conjecture and partial restrictions on the set. It does not determine membership for every positive eta or settle whether the set is empty.
